reuse.why: The range rule is centralised in a new getRangeAmount that getScheduledAmount also uses, but the server sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount, which already decides all three cases.

duplication.why: No new copy of the range arithmetic, but the `null ? 0 : number ? v : range` dispatch stays repeated at four sites (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, normalizeSchedule) next to a helper that already does it.

placement.why: getRangeAmount lives in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount, where schedule amount logic belongs, and is imported by server modules.

scope.why: Only the range rule, its call sites, comments, tests and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: A future change to the range rule is one edit, though maintainers still face two layers (getRangeAmount and getScheduledAmount) and repeated dispatch; one comment is awkwardly line-broken.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts createScheduleList, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions resolve the amount themselves instead of calling getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic is disguised; the remaining per-site dispatch ternaries are the pre-existing ones left in place.

one_place.where: The worst-case rule is defined once in getRangeAmount (shared/schedules.ts), used by getScheduledAmount and by every server site that previously computed the midpoint.
